```{r importData, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

# subset out male and female populations

male_2018 <- subset(ocme_2018, Sex_revised == "Male")
female_2018 <- subset(ocme_2018, Sex_revised == "Female")

female_2019 <- subset(ocme_2019, Sex_revised == "Female")

female_2020 <- subset(ocme_2020, Sex_revised == "Female")

female_2021 <- subset(ocme_2021, Sex_revised == "Female")

female_2022 <- subset(ocme_2022, Sex_revised == "Female")

female_2023 <- subset(ocme_2023, Sex_revised == "Female")

# subset out populations by race

white_2018 <- subset(ocme_2018, race_numeric_words == "White")

black_2019 <- subset(ocme_2019, race_numeric_words == "Black")
latine_2019 <- subset(ocme_2019, race_numeric_words == "Hispanic")

white_2020 <- subset(ocme_2020, race_numeric_words == "White")
black_2020 <- subset(ocme_2020, race_numeric_words == "Black")
latine_2020 <- subset(ocme_2020, race_numeric_words == "Hispanic")

white_2021 <- subset(ocme_2021, race_numeric_words == "White")
black_2021 <- subset(ocme_2021, race_numeric_words == "Black")
latine_2021 <- subset(ocme_2021, race_numeric_words == "Hispanic")

white_2022 <- subset(ocme_2022, race_numeric_words == "White")
black_2022 <- subset(ocme_2022, race_numeric_words == "Black")
latine_2022 <- subset(ocme_2022, race_numeric_words == "Hispanic")

white_2023 <- subset(ocme_2023, race_numeric_words == "White")
black_2023 <- subset(ocme_2023, race_numeric_words == "Black")
latine_2023 <- subset(ocme_2023, race_numeric_words == "Hispanic")


# import SWORD data

sword <- read.csv("data_preprocessing/processed_data/sword_processed.csv")
sword_2020 <- subset(sword, Year == "2020")
sword_2021 <- subset(sword, Year == "2021")
sword_2022 <- subset(sword, Year == "2022")
sword_2023 <- subset(sword, Year == "2023")

# import city and county population data

county_pop_2018 <- read.csv("data_preprocessing/processed_data/county_pop_2018_processed.csv")
county_pop_2019 <- read.csv("data_preprocessing/processed_data/county_pop_2019_processed.csv")
county_pop_2020 <- read.csv("data_preprocessing/processed_data/county_pop_2020_processed.csv")
county_pop_2021 <- read.csv("data_preprocessing/processed_data/county_pop_2021_processed.csv")
county_pop_2022 <- read.csv("data_preprocessing/processed_data/county_pop_2022_processed.csv")
county_pop_2023 <- read.csv("data_preprocessing/processed_data/county_pop_2023_processed.csv")


city_pop_2018 <- read.csv("data_preprocessing/processed_data/city_pop_2018_processed.csv")
city_pop_2019 <- read.csv("data_preprocessing/processed_data/city_pop_2019_processed.csv")

city_pop_2021 <- read.csv("data_preprocessing/processed_data/city_pop_2021_processed.csv")
city_pop_2022 <- read.csv("data_preprocessing/processed_data/city_pop_2022_processed.csv")
city_pop_2023 <- read.csv("data_preprocessing/processed_data/city_pop_2023_processed.csv")


# I don't think this needs preprocessing--import data on population by race/age for age-adjustment

race_age_pop <- read.csv("data_preprocessing/pop_files/race_age_pop.csv")

# get town data from tigris so we can map deaths by town later

options(tigris_use_cache=TRUE)
ct_towns = county_subdivisions(state="Connecticut")
ct_towns$NAME = str_to_title(ct_towns$NAME)
ct_towns = filter(ct_towns, NAME != "County Subdivisions Not Defined")
# tigris also has shapefiles for the long island sound so let's get rid of that
ct_towns <- subset(ct_towns, ALAND!=0)

```

### Age distribution for all fatal and nonfatal overdoses {.tabset}

#### 2018

```{r age2018, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
#there was an issue with the x axis not showing up when I coped the other histogram code -- resolved using https://stackoverflow.com/questions/42425195/ggplot-data-year-over-year-axis-labels-not-showing

#fixed issue with colors not showing -- turns out it was because the data was numeric: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/55400037/ggplot-geom-bar-fill-not-coloring-bars-on-plot

#calculate modes, see https://stackoverflow.com/questions/27418461/calculate-the-modes-in-a-multimodal-distribution-in-r

# Select an appropriate bandwidth. Here we use a "rule of thumb" method
# looks like there are some NAs in the 2018 data so I have to get rid of them
bandwidth <- bw.nrd0(na.omit(ocme_2018$age)) 

# Other methods, e.g. bw.ucv(), will identify different bandwidths as optimal
# Consequently the number (and position) of modes may differ too

# Methods implemented in multimode are documented at ?bw.nrd

# Calculate number of modes
n <- nmodes(ocme_2018$age, bw = bandwidth)

# Calculate location of these modes
loc <- locmodes(ocme_2018$age, mod0 = n, display=TRUE)
# Remove `, display = TRUE` if you don't want to see the KDE
#loc

# Locations of modes are odd values in loc
modes <- loc$locations[seq(from = 1, by = 2, length.out = n)]
antimodes <- loc$locations[seq(from = 0, by = 2, length.out = n)]

# subset out "young" and "old" populations -- "young" is <= first antimode, "old" is > first antimode
ocme_2018_young <- subset(ocme_2018, age <= antimodes[1])
ocme_2018_old <- subset(ocme_2018, age > antimodes[1])

# create a condition to use different colors based on the location of the antimode
# from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/13372523/altering-the-color-of-one-value-in-a-ggplot-histogram
# it just gives me a 0 for anything in the younger population, 1 for older

ocme_2018$aftermode <- ocme_2018$age > antimodes[1]

#added multiple mode lines to plot using https://stackoverflow.com/questions/71580196/add-horizontal-lines-from-a-vector-to-a-ggplot-uisng-facet-grid


# a plot without mode lines or anything, with the number of people dying for each age 
ggplot(data=ocme_2018, aes(x=age, ..count..)) + 
      geom_bar(aes(fill = as.character(aftermode)), position = "dodge") + scale_x_continuous(guide = guide_axis(angle = 90), breaks = ocme_2018$age, labels = ocme_2018$age) + geom_text(aes(label = ..count..), stat = "count", vjust = 0, colour = "black", size = 7/.pt) + theme_light() + ggtitle("Age distribution for 2018 CT opioid-detected overdose deaths")+theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5), legend.position="right", axis.text.x = element_text(size = 7)) + scale_fill_manual(name = "Age group", values = c("#00BFC4", "#F8766D"), labels = c("Younger", "Older"))+xlab("Age")+ylab("Number of decedents")

age_2018 <- ggplot(data=ocme_2018, aes(x=age, ..count..)) + 
      geom_bar(aes(fill = as.character(aftermode)), position = "dodge") + scale_x_continuous(guide = guide_axis(angle = 90), breaks = ocme_2018$age, labels = ocme_2018$age) + theme_light() + geom_vline(xintercept = modes, size=1) + ggtitle("Age distribution for 2018 CT opioid-detected overdose deaths")+theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5), legend.position="right", axis.text.x = element_text(size = 7)) + scale_fill_manual(name = "Age group", values = c("#00BFC4", "#F8766D"), labels = c("Younger", "Older"))+xlab("Age")+ylab("Number of decedents")

age_2018

ggsave(plot=age_2018, filename = "images/age_2018.png", width = 10, height = 8)


sprintf("Using Hartigan's dip test for bimodality, the resulting p value is %f.", dip.test(ocme_2018$age)$p.value) 

 
```

```{r ageSWORD2021, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
#fixed issue with colors not showing -- turns out it was because the data was numeric: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/55400037/ggplot-geom-bar-fill-not-coloring-bars-on-plot

#calculate modes, see https://stackoverflow.com/questions/27418461/calculate-the-modes-in-a-multimodal-distribution-in-r

# Select an appropriate bandwidth. Here we use a "rule of thumb" method
bandwidth <- bw.nrd0(sword_2021$Age) 

# Other methods, e.g. bw.ucv(), will identify different bandwidths as optimal
# Consequently the number (and position) of modes may differ too

# Methods implemented in multimode are documented at ?bw.nrd

# Calculate number of modes
n <- nmodes(sword_2021$Age, bw = bandwidth)

# Calculate location of these modes
loc <- locmodes(sword_2021$Age, mod0 = n, display=TRUE)
# Remove `, display = TRUE` if you don't want to see the KDE
#loc

# Locations of modes are odd values in loc
modes <- loc$locations[seq(from = 1, by = 2, length.out = n)]
antimodes <- loc$locations[seq(from = 0, by = 2, length.out = n)]

# subset out "young" and "old" populations -- "young" is <= first antimode, "old" is > first antimode
sword_2021_young <- subset(sword_2021, Age <= antimodes[1])
sword_2021_old <- subset(sword_2021, Age > antimodes[1])


# create a condition to use different colors based on the location of the antimode
# from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/13372523/altering-the-color-of-one-value-in-a-ggplot-histogram
# it just gives me a 0 for anything in the younger population, 1 for older

sword_2021$aftermode <- sword_2021$Age > antimodes[1]

#added multiple mode lines to plot using https://stackoverflow.com/questions/71580196/add-horizontal-lines-from-a-vector-to-a-ggplot-uisng-facet-grid


# a plot without mode lines or anything, with the number of people dying for each age 
ggplot(data=sword_2021, aes(x=Age, ..count..)) + 
      geom_bar(aes(fill = as.character(aftermode)), position = "dodge") + scale_x_continuous(guide = guide_axis(angle = 90), breaks = sword_2021$Age, labels = sword_2021$Age) + geom_text(aes(label = ..count..), stat = "count", vjust = 0, colour = "black", size = 7/.pt) + theme_light() + ggtitle("Age distribution for 2021 nonfatal opioid-involved overdoses in CT")+theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5), legend.position="right", axis.text.x = element_text(size = 7)) + scale_fill_manual(name = "Age group", values = c("#00BFC4", "#F8766D"), labels = c("Younger", "Older"))+xlab("Age")+ylab("Number of overdoses")

age_2021 <- ggplot(data=sword_2021, aes(x=Age, ..count..)) + 
      geom_bar(aes(fill = as.character(aftermode)), position = "dodge") + scale_x_continuous(guide = guide_axis(angle = 90), breaks = sword_2021$Age, labels = sword_2021$Age) + theme_light() + geom_vline(xintercept = modes, size=1) + ggtitle("Age distribution for 2021 nonfatal opioid-involved overdoses in CT")+theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5), legend.position="right", axis.text.x = element_text(size = 7)) + scale_fill_manual(name = "Age group", values = c("#00BFC4", "#F8766D"), labels = c("Younger", "Older"))+xlab("Age")+ylab("Number of overdoess")
age_2021

ggsave(plot=age_2021, filename = "images/age_sword_2021.png", width = 10, height = 8)

sprintf("Using Hartigan's dip test for bimodality, the resulting p value is %f.", dip.test(sword_2021$Age)$p.value) 

 
```

### Age distribution for white people {.tabset}

#### 2018

```{r age2018White, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
#there was an issue with the x axis not showing up when I coped the other histogram code -- resolved using https://stackoverflow.com/questions/42425195/ggplot-data-year-over-year-axis-labels-not-showing

#fixed issue with colors not showing -- turns out it was because the data was numeric: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/55400037/ggplot-geom-bar-fill-not-coloring-bars-on-plot

#calculate modes, see https://stackoverflow.com/questions/27418461/calculate-the-modes-in-a-multimodal-distribution-in-r

# Select an appropriate bandwidth. Here we use a "rule of thumb" method
# looks like there are some NAs in the 2018 data so I have to get rid of them
bandwidth <- bw.nrd0(na.omit(white_2018$age)) 

# Other methods, e.g. bw.ucv(), will identify different bandwidths as optimal
# Consequently the number (and position) of modes may differ too

# Methods implemented in multimode are documented at ?bw.nrd

# Calculate number of modes
n <- nmodes(white_2018$age, bw = bandwidth)

# Calculate location of these modes
loc <- locmodes(white_2018$age, mod0 = n, display=TRUE)
# Remove `, display = TRUE` if you don't want to see the KDE
#loc

# Locations of modes are odd values in loc
modes <- loc$locations[seq(from = 1, by = 2, length.out = n)]
antimodes <- loc$locations[seq(from = 0, by = 2, length.out = n)]

# subset out "young" and "old" populations -- "young" is <= first antimode, "old" is > first antimode
white_2018_young <- subset(white_2018, age <= antimodes[1])
white_2018_old <- subset(white_2018, age > antimodes[1])

#added multiple mode lines to plot using https://stackoverflow.com/questions/71580196/add-horizontal-lines-from-a-vector-to-a-ggplot-uisng-facet-grid


# a plot without mode lines or anything, with the number of people dying for each age 
ggplot(data=white_2018, aes(x=age, ..count..)) + 
      geom_bar(aes(fill = as.character(age)), position = "dodge") + scale_x_continuous(guide = guide_axis(angle = 90), breaks = white_2018$age, labels = white_2018$age) + geom_text(aes(label = ..count..), stat = "count", vjust = 0, colour = "black", size = 7/.pt) + theme_light() + ggtitle("Age distribution for 2018 opioid-detected deaths in white people")+theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5), legend.position="none", axis.text.x = element_text(size = 7))

age_2018 <- ggplot(data=white_2018, aes(x=age, ..count..)) + 
      geom_bar(aes(fill = as.character(age)), position = "dodge") + scale_x_continuous(guide = guide_axis(angle = 90), breaks = white_2018$age, labels = white_2018$age) + theme_light() + geom_vline(xintercept = modes[-length(modes)], size=1) + ggtitle("Age distribution for 2018 opioid-detected deaths in white people")+theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5), legend.position="none", axis.text.x = element_text(size = 7))

age_2018

ggsave(plot=age_2018, filename = "images/age_2018_white.png", width = 10, height = 8)


sprintf("Using Hartigan's dip test for bimodality, the resulting p value is %f.", dip.test(white_2018$age)$p.value)
```

```{r age2020White, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
#there was an issue with the x axis not showing up when I coped the other histogram code -- resolved using https://stackoverflow.com/questions/42425195/ggplot-data-year-over-year-axis-labels-not-showing

#fixed issue with colors not showing -- turns out it was because the data was numeric: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/55400037/ggplot-geom-bar-fill-not-coloring-bars-on-plot

#calculate modes, see https://stackoverflow.com/questions/27418461/calculate-the-modes-in-a-multimodal-distribution-in-r

# Select an appropriate bandwidth. Here we use a "rule of thumb" method
bandwidth <- bw.nrd0(white_2020$age) 

# Other methods, e.g. bw.ucv(), will identify different bandwidths as optimal
# Consequently the number (and position) of modes may differ too

# Methods implemented in multimode are documented at ?bw.nrd

# Calculate number of modes
n <- nmodes(white_2020$age, bw = bandwidth)

# Calculate location of these modes
loc <- locmodes(white_2020$age, mod0 = n, display=TRUE)
# Remove `, display = TRUE` if you don't want to see the KDE
#loc

# Locations of modes are odd values in loc
modes <- loc$locations[seq(from = 1, by = 2, length.out = n)]
antimodes <- loc$locations[seq(from = 0, by = 2, length.out = n)]

# subset out "young" and "old" populations -- "young" is <= first antimode, "old" is > first antimode
white_2020_young <- subset(white_2020, age <= antimodes[1])
white_2020_old <- subset(white_2020, age > antimodes[1])

#added multiple mode lines to plot using https://stackoverflow.com/questions/71580196/add-horizontal-lines-from-a-vector-to-a-ggplot-uisng-facet-grid


# a plot without mode lines or anything, with the number of people dying for each age 
ggplot(data=white_2020, aes(x=age, ..count..)) + 
      geom_bar(aes(fill = as.character(age)), position = "dodge") + scale_x_continuous(guide = guide_axis(angle = 90), breaks = white_2020$age, labels = white_2020$age) + geom_text(aes(label = ..count..), stat = "count", vjust = 0, colour = "black", size = 7/.pt) + theme_light() + ggtitle("Age distribution for 2020 opioid-detected deaths in white people")+theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5), legend.position="none", axis.text.x = element_text(size = 7))

age_2020 <- ggplot(data=white_2020, aes(x=age, ..count..)) + 
      geom_bar(aes(fill = as.character(age)), position = "dodge") + scale_x_continuous(guide = guide_axis(angle = 90), breaks = white_2020$age, labels = white_2020$age) + theme_light() + geom_vline(xintercept = modes, size=1) + ggtitle("Age distribution for 2020 opioid-detected deaths in white people")+theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5), legend.position="none", axis.text.x = element_text(size = 7))

age_2020

ggsave(plot=age_2020, filename = "images/age_2020_white.png", width = 10, height = 8)

sprintf("Using Hartigan's dip test for bimodality, the resulting p value is %f.", dip.test(white_2020$age)$p.value) 


```

#### 2021

```{r age2021Female, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
#there was an issue with the x axis not showing up when I coped the other histogram code -- resolved using https://stackoverflow.com/questions/42425195/ggplot-data-year-over-year-axis-labels-not-showing

#fixed issue with colors not showing -- turns out it was because the data was numeric: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/55400037/ggplot-geom-bar-fill-not-coloring-bars-on-plot

#calculate modes, see https://stackoverflow.com/questions/27418461/calculate-the-modes-in-a-multimodal-distribution-in-r

# Select an appropriate bandwidth. Here we use a "rule of thumb" method
bandwidth <- bw.nrd0(female_2021$age) 

# Other methods, e.g. bw.ucv(), will identify different bandwidths as optimal
# Consequently the number (and position) of modes may differ too

# Methods implemented in multimode are documented at ?bw.nrd

# Calculate number of modes
n <- nmodes(female_2021$age, bw = bandwidth)

# Calculate location of these modes
loc <- locmodes(female_2021$age, mod0 = n, display=TRUE)
# Remove `, display = TRUE` if you don't want to see the KDE
#loc

# Locations of modes are odd values in loc
modes <- loc$locations[seq(from = 1, by = 2, length.out = n)]
antimodes <- loc$locations[seq(from = 0, by = 2, length.out = n)]

# subset out "young" and "old" populations -- "young" is <= first antimode, "old" is > first antimode
female_2021_young <- subset(female_2021, age <= antimodes[1])
female_2021_old <- subset(female_2021, age > antimodes[1])

#added multiple mode lines to plot using https://stackoverflow.com/questions/71580196/add-horizontal-lines-from-a-vector-to-a-ggplot-uisng-facet-grid


# a plot without mode lines or anything, with the number of people dying for each age 
ggplot(data=female_2021, aes(x=age, ..count..)) + 
      geom_bar(aes(fill = as.character(age)), position = "dodge") + scale_x_continuous(guide = guide_axis(angle = 90), breaks = female_2021$age, labels = female_2021$age) + geom_text(aes(label = ..count..), stat = "count", vjust = 0, colour = "black", size = 7/.pt) + theme_light() + ggtitle("Age distribution for 2021 opioid-detected deaths in women")+theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5), legend.position="none", axis.text.x = element_text(size = 7))

age_2021 <- ggplot(data=female_2021, aes(x=age, ..count..)) + 
      geom_bar(aes(fill = as.character(age)), position = "dodge") + scale_x_continuous(guide = guide_axis(angle = 90), breaks = female_2021$age, labels = female_2021$age) + theme_light() + geom_vline(xintercept = modes, size=1) + ggtitle("Age distribution for 2021 opioid-detected deaths in women")+theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5), legend.position="none", axis.text.x = element_text(size = 7))
age_2021
```

```{r age2023Female, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

antimodes <- loc$locations[seq(from = 0, by = 2, length.out = n)]

female_2023_old <- subset(female_2023, age > antimodes[2])
```

### Median age

**Fatal**

```{r median, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
sprintf("The median age of decedents in 2018 was %d. For younger decedents the median age was %d and for older decedents the median age was %d.", median(ocme_2018$age), median(ocme_2018_young$age), median(ocme_2018_old$age))

sprintf("The median age of decedents in 2019 was %d. For younger decedents the median age was %d and for older decedents the median age was %d.", median(ocme_2019$age), median(ocme_2019_young$age), median(ocme_2019_old$age))

sprintf("The median age of decedents in 2020 was %d. For younger decedents the median age was %d and for older decedents the median age was %d.", median(ocme_2020$age), median(ocme_2020_young$age), median(ocme_2020_old$age))

sprintf("The median age of decedents in 2021 was %d. For younger decedents the median age was %d and for older decedents the median age was %d.", median(ocme_2021$age), median(ocme_2021_young$age), median(ocme_2021_old$age))

sprintf("The median age of decedents in 2022 was %d. For younger decedents the median age was %d and for older decedents the median age was %d.", median(ocme_2022$age), median(ocme_2022_young$age), median(ocme_2022_old$age))

sprintf("The median age of decedents in 2023 was %d. For younger decedents the median age was %d and for older decedents the median age was %d.", median(ocme_2023$age), median(ocme_2023_young$age), median(ocme_2023_old$age))
```

**Nonfatal**

```{r medianSWORD, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
sprintf("The median age of nonfatal ODs in 2020 was %d. For younger people the median age was %d and for older decedents the people age was %d.", median(sword_2020$Age), median(sword_2020_young$age), median(sword_2020_old$age))

sprintf("The median age of nonfatal ODs in 2021 was %d. For younger pwoplw the median age was %d and for older pwoplw the median age was %d.", median(sword_2021$Age), median(sword_2021_young$age), median(sword_2021_old$age))
```

### Chi squared testing for race {.tabset}

#### 2018

```{r chiSquaredRace2018, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# getting this from https://www.datacamp.com/tutorial/chi-square-test-r

# get frequency of each race for old and young, from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/48562288/frequency-of-each-unique-combination-in-data-frame

racefreqtable <- ocme_2018_young %>% group_by(race_numeric_words) %>% tally()
names(racefreqtable)[names(racefreqtable) == 'n'] <- 'Young'

racetableold <- ocme_2018_old %>% group_by(race_numeric_words) %>% tally()
names(racetableold)[names(racetableold) == 'n'] <- 'Old'

racetable2018 <- merge(racefreqtable, racetableold, by="race_numeric_words")

# convert the "race" column into row names so I get a table with only numeric values, from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/5555408/convert-the-values-in-a-column-into-row-names-in-an-existing-data-frame

racemat2018 <- racetable2018[,-1]
rownames(racemat2018) <- racetable2018[,1]

as.matrix(racemat2018)

# looks like I can just use any matrix for chisq.test, from https://researchguides.library.vanderbilt.edu/c.php?g=156859&p=3058795

chisq.test(as.matrix(racemat2018))
```

### Chi squared testing for sex of decedents {.tabset}

#### 2018

```{r chiSquaredSex2018, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# get frequency of each race for old and young, from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/48562288/frequency-of-each-unique-combination-in-data-frame

sexfreqtable <- ocme_2018_young %>% group_by(Sex_revised) %>% tally()
names(sexfreqtable)[names(sexfreqtable) == 'n'] <- 'Young'

sextableold <- ocme_2018_old %>% group_by(Sex_revised) %>% tally()
names(sextableold)[names(sextableold) == 'n'] <- 'Old'

sextable2018 <- merge(sexfreqtable, sextableold, by="Sex_revised")

# convert the "sex" column into row names so I get a table with only numeric values, from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/5555408/convert-the-values-in-a-column-into-row-names-in-an-existing-data-frame

sexmat2018 <- sextable2018[,-1]
rownames(sexmat2018) <- sextable2018[,1]

as.matrix(sexmat2018)

# looks like I can just use any matrix for chisq.test, from https://researchguides.library.vanderbilt.edu/c.php?g=156859&p=3058795

chisq.test(as.matrix(sexmat2018))
```

```{r chiSquaredSex2022, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# get frequency of each race for old and young, from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/48562288/frequency-of-each-unique-combination-in-data-frame

sexfreqtable <- ocme_2022_young %>% group_by(Sex_revised) %>% tally()
names(sexfreqtable)[names(sexfreqtable) == 'n'] <- 'Young'

sextableold <- ocme_2022_old %>% group_by(Sex_revised) %>% tally()
names(sextableold)[names(sextableold) == 'n'] <- 'Old'

sextable2022 <- merge(sexfreqtable, sextableold, by="Sex_revised")

# convert the "sex" column into row names so I get a table with only numeric values, from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/5555408/convert-the-values-in-a-column-into-row-names-in-an-existing-data-frame

sexmat2022 <- sextable2022[,-1]
rownames(sexmat2022) <- sextable2022[,1]

as.matrix(sexmat2022)

# looks like I can just use any matrix for chisq.test, from https://researchguides.library.vanderbilt.edu/c.php?g=156859&p=3058795

chisq.test(as.matrix(sexmat2022))
```

### Race and sex of decedents {.tabset}

#### 2018

**Young**

```{r sexRaceTableYoung2018, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
raceSex2018 <- ggplot(data=ocme_2018_young, aes(x=race_sex, ..count..)) + 
      geom_bar(aes(fill = race_sex), position = "dodge") + scale_x_discrete(guide = guide_axis(angle = 45)) + theme_light() + geom_text(aes(label = ..count..), stat = "count", vjust = 0, colour = "black")+ ggtitle("Race/ethnicity and sex distribution for 2018 CT opioid-detected \n overdose deaths in younger people")+ theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5), legend.position="none")

raceSex2018

ggsave(plot=raceSex2018, filename = "images/raceSex2018_young.png", width = 10, height = 8)

raceSexProp2018 <- ggplot(data=ocme_2018_young, aes(x=race_sex, ..count..)) + 
      geom_bar(aes(fill = race_sex), position = "dodge") + scale_x_discrete(guide = guide_axis(angle = 45)) + theme_light() + geom_text(aes(label = round(..count../nrow(ocme_2018_young), 3)), stat = "count", vjust = 0, colour = "black")+ ggtitle("Race/ethnicity and sex distribution for 2018 CT opioid-detected \n overdose deaths in younger people") + theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5), legend.position="none")

raceSexProp2018
ggsave(plot=raceSexProp2018, filename = "images/raceSexProp2018_young.png", width = 10, height = 8)

# pie chart info from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/45657990/how-to-create-a-pie-chart-with-percentage-labels-using-ggplot2

# ggrepel info from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/69715282/how-to-adjust-ggrepel-label-on-pie-chart

# get the % of each race sex category
ocme_2018_younglong <- ocme_2018_young %>% 
  group_by(race_sex) %>% 
  count() %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  mutate(per=`n`/sum(`n`)) %>% 
  arrange(desc(race_sex))
# create a label out of this
ocme_2018_younglong$racesexlabel <- scales::percent(ocme_2018_younglong$per)


# automatically assign the color based on race sex value
# from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/39142596/r-ggplot-set-colour-for-specific-value

ocme_2018_younglong$color <- ifelse(ocme_2018_younglong$race_sex == "Black Female", "#e6d0a1", ifelse(ocme_2018_younglong$race_sex == "Black Male", "#E69F00", ifelse(ocme_2018_younglong$race_sex == "Hispanic Female", "#b3d4e8", ifelse(ocme_2018_younglong$race_sex == "Hispanic Male", "#56B4E9", ifelse(ocme_2018_younglong$race_sex == "Other Female", "#cca1b9", ifelse(ocme_2018_younglong$race_sex == "Other Male", "#CC79A7", ifelse(ocme_2018_younglong$race_sex == "White Female", "#a1a1a1", ifelse(ocme_2018_younglong$race_sex == "White Male", "#000000", "yellow"))))))))


# plot into a pie chart -- for some reason I have to reverse the color and labels
pie2018young <- ggplot(data=ocme_2018_younglong)+
  geom_bar(aes(x="", y=per, fill=race_sex), stat="identity", width = 1)+
  coord_polar("y", start=0)+
  theme_void()+ geom_label_repel(aes(label = racesexlabel, x = "", y = cumsum(per) - per/2), nudge_x = 0.02,
                   size = 3, show.legend = F)+  scale_fill_manual(name = "Race/ethnicity and sex", values = rev(ocme_2018_younglong$color), labels = rev(ocme_2018_younglong$race_sex)) + ggtitle("Race/ethnicity and sex distribution for 2018 CT opioid-detected \n overdose deaths in younger people") + theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5), legend.position="right") 
# geom_text(aes(x=1, y = cumsum(per) - per/2, label=label)) for regular labels [not repelling]

pie2018young

ggsave(plot=pie2018young, filename = "images/pie2018_young.png", width = 10, height = 8)

```

```{r sexRaceTableYoung2023, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
raceSex2023
```

```{r sexRaceTableOld2023, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
raceSexProp2023 <- ggplot(data=ocme_2023_old, aes(x=race_sex, ..count..)) + 
      geom_bar(aes(fill = race_sex), position = "dodge") + scale_x_discrete(guide = guide_axis(angle = 45)) + theme_light() + geom_text(aes(label = round(..count../nrow(ocme_2023_old), 3)), stat = "count", vjust = 0, colour = "black")+ ggtitle("Race/sex distribution for 2023 CT opioid-detected \n overdose deaths in older people") + theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5), legend.position="none") 

raceSexProp2023

# pie chart info from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/45657990/how-to-create-a-pie-chart-with-percentage-labels-using-ggplot2

# ggrepel info from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/69715282/how-to-adjust-ggrepel-label-on-pie-chart

# get the % of each race sex category
ocme_2023_oldlong <- ocme_2023_old %>% 
  group_by(race_sex) %>% 
  count() %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  mutate(per=`n`/sum(`n`)) %>% 
  arrange(desc(race_sex))
# create a label out of this
ocme_2023_oldlong$racesexlabel <- scales::percent(ocme_2023_oldlong$per)


# automatically assign the color based on race sex value
# from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/39142596/r-ggplot-set-colour-for-specific-value

ocme_2023_oldlong$color <- ifelse(ocme_2023_oldlong$race_sex == "Black Female", "#e6d0a1", ifelse(ocme_2023_oldlong$race_sex == "Black Male", "#E69F00", ifelse(ocme_2023_oldlong$race_sex == "Hispanic Female", "#b3d4e8", ifelse(ocme_2023_oldlong$race_sex == "Hispanic Male", "#56B4E9", ifelse(ocme_2023_oldlong$race_sex == "Other Female", "#cca1b9", ifelse(ocme_2023_oldlong$race_sex == "Other Male", "#CC79A7", ifelse(ocme_2023_oldlong$race_sex == "White Female", "#a1a1a1", ifelse(ocme_2023_oldlong$race_sex == "White Male", "#000000", "yellow"))))))))


# plot into a pie chart -- for some reason I have to reverse the color and labels
pie2023old <- ggplot(data=ocme_2023_oldlong)+
  geom_bar(aes(x="", y=per, fill=race_sex), stat="identity", width = 1)+
  coord_polar("y", start=0)+
  theme_void()+ geom_label_repel(aes(label = racesexlabel, x = "", y = cumsum(per) - per/2), nudge_x = 0.02,
                   size = 3, show.legend = F)+  scale_fill_manual(name = "Race/ethnicity and sex", values = rev(ocme_2023_oldlong$color), labels = rev(ocme_2023_oldlong$race_sex)) + ggtitle("Race/sex distribution for 2023 CT opioid-detected \n overdose deaths in older people") + theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5), legend.position="right") 
# geom_text(aes(x=1, y = cumsum(per) - per/2, label=label)) for regular labels [not repelling]

pie2023old

ggsave(plot=pie2023old, filename = "images/pie2023_old.png", width = 10, height = 8)

```


### Chi squared testing for race and sex {.tabset}

#### 2018

```{r chiSquaredRaceSex2018, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# get frequency of each race for old and young, from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/48562288/frequency-of-each-unique-combination-in-data-frame

racesexfreqtable <- ocme_2018_young %>% group_by(race_sex) %>% tally()
names(racesexfreqtable)[names(racesexfreqtable) == 'n'] <- 'Young'

racesextableold <- ocme_2018_old %>% group_by(race_sex) %>% tally()
names(racesextableold)[names(racesextableold) == 'n'] <- 'Old'

racesextable2018 <- merge(racesexfreqtable, racesextableold, by="race_sex")

# convert the "race_sex" column into row names so I get a table with only numeric values, from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/5555408/convert-the-values-in-a-column-into-row-names-in-an-existing-data-frame

racesexmat2018 <- racesextable2018[,-1]
rownames(racesexmat2018) <- racesextable2018[,1]

as.matrix(racesexmat2018)

# looks like I can just use any matrix for chisq.test, from https://researchguides.library.vanderbilt.edu/c.php?g=156859&p=3058795

chisq.test(as.matrix(racesexmat2018))
```

### Chi squared testing for day of week for decedents {.tabset}

#### 2018

```{r chiSquaredWeekday2018, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# get frequency of each race for old and young, from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/48562288/frequency-of-each-unique-combination-in-data-frame

weekdayfreqtable <- ocme_2018_young %>% group_by(Weekday) %>% tally()
names(weekdayfreqtable)[names(weekdayfreqtable) == 'n'] <- 'Young'

weekdaytableold <- ocme_2018_old %>% group_by(Weekday) %>% tally()
names(weekdaytableold)[names(weekdaytableold) == 'n'] <- 'Old'

weekdaytable2018 <- merge(weekdayfreqtable, weekdaytableold, by="Weekday")

# convert the "race_sex" column into row names so I get a table with only numeric values, from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/5555408/convert-the-values-in-a-column-into-row-names-in-an-existing-data-frame

weekdaymat2018 <- weekdaytable2018[,-1]
rownames(weekdaymat2018) <- weekdaytable2018[,1]

as.matrix(weekdaymat2018)

# looks like I can just use any matrix for chisq.test, from https://researchguides.library.vanderbilt.edu/c.php?g=156859&p=3058795

chisq.test(as.matrix(weekdaymat2018))
```

### Chi squared testing for month for decedents {.tabset}

#### 2018

```{r chiSquaredMonth2018, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# get frequency of each race for old and young, from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/48562288/frequency-of-each-unique-combination-in-data-frame

monthfreqtable <- ocme_2018_young %>% group_by(month) %>% tally()
names(monthfreqtable)[names(monthfreqtable) == 'n'] <- 'Young'

monthtableold <- ocme_2018_old %>% group_by(month) %>% tally()
names(monthtableold)[names(monthtableold) == 'n'] <- 'Old'

monthtable2018 <- merge(monthfreqtable, monthtableold, by="month")

# convert the "race_sex" column into row names so I get a table with only numeric values, from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/5555408/convert-the-values-in-a-column-into-row-names-in-an-existing-data-frame

monthmat2018 <- monthtable2018[,-1]
rownames(monthmat2018) <- monthtable2018[,1]

as.matrix(monthmat2018)

# looks like I can just use any matrix for chisq.test, from https://researchguides.library.vanderbilt.edu/c.php?g=156859&p=3058795

chisq.test(as.matrix(monthmat2018))
```

### Proportion of deaths involving fentanyl

Is this a reasonable way to display the data? I know the antimode changes year to year so this is not as effective a comparison as it could be. 

```{r propFent, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

year <- c(2018, 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023)


# unfortunately there are different variable names for each ocme file so a for loop won't work :/

# get proportion of fent for each year for younger people -- from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/28195996/count-number-of-rows-matching-a-criteria
fentyoung <- c(sum(ocme_2018_young$fent.or.frankens == 1)/nrow(ocme_2018_young), sum(ocme_2019_young$fent...frankens == 1)/nrow(ocme_2019_young), sum(ocme_2020_young$fent...frankens == 1)/nrow(ocme_2020_young), sum(ocme_2021_young$fent...frankens == 1)/nrow(ocme_2021_young), sum(ocme_2022_young$fent...frankens == 1)/nrow(ocme_2022_young), sum(ocme_2023_young$fent...frankens ==1)/nrow(ocme_2023_young))

# get proportion for older people
fentold <- c(sum(ocme_2018_old$fent.or.frankens == 1)/nrow(ocme_2018_old), sum(ocme_2019_old$fent...frankens == 1)/nrow(ocme_2019_old), sum(ocme_2020_old$fent...frankens == 1)/nrow(ocme_2020_old), sum(ocme_2021_old$fent...frankens == 1)/nrow(ocme_2021_old), sum(ocme_2022_old$fent...frankens == 1)/nrow(ocme_2022_old), sum(ocme_2023_old$fent...frankens ==1)/nrow(ocme_2023_old))

# combine vectors into df
propfent <- data.frame(year, fentyoung, fentold)

# change the col names to be more informative
names(propfent) <- c("Year", "Younger", "Older")

# create grouped bar plot, from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/72449952/making-a-grouped-bar-chart-in-r
# getting the labels in the right position from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/37587288/ggplot-label-bars-in-grouped-bar-plot
# info on changing legend title from here https://stackoverflow.com/questions/41649929/how-to-modify-a-legend-title-in-a-barplot-with-ggplot
# the scale x continuous is there because for some reason adding 2023 data messed up the x axis, see https://stackoverflow.com/questions/72051789/how-to-display-all-values-on-x-and-y-axes-in-r-ggplot2

pfent <- propfent |>
  # Reshape data to long format
  pivot_longer(Younger:Older) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = Year, y = value, fill = name)) +
  # Implement a grouped bar chart
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = position_dodge(width= 1)) + geom_text(aes(label = round(value, 2)), stat = "identity", vjust = -0.1, colour = "black", size = 9/.pt, position = position_dodge(width= 1)) + theme_light() + ggtitle("Proportion of fentanyl-detected deaths by age group in CT, 2018-2023") + ylab("Proportion") + theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)) + scale_fill_discrete(name = "age group") + coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1)) + scale_x_continuous(breaks=propfent$Year) 

pfent

ggsave(plot=pfent, filename = "images/prop_fent.png", width = 10, height = 8)
```

### Proportion of deaths involving alcohol

```{r propEtoh, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

year <- c(2018, 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023)

# unfortunately there are different variable names for each ocme file so a for loop won't work :/

# get proportion of cocaine for each year for younger people -- from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/28195996/count-number-of-rows-matching-a-criteria
etohyoung <- c(sum(ocme_2018_young$EtOH == 1)/nrow(ocme_2018_young), sum(ocme_2019_young$EtOH == 1)/nrow(ocme_2019_young), sum(ocme_2020_young$EtOH == 1)/nrow(ocme_2020_young), sum(ocme_2021_young$EtOH == 1)/nrow(ocme_2021_young), sum(ocme_2022_young$EtOH == 1)/nrow(ocme_2022_young), sum(ocme_2023_young$EtOH == 1)/nrow(ocme_2023_young))

# get proportion for older people
etohold <- c(sum(ocme_2018_old$EtOH == 1)/nrow(ocme_2018_old), sum(ocme_2019_old$EtOH == 1)/nrow(ocme_2019_old), sum(ocme_2020_old$EtOH == 1)/nrow(ocme_2020_old), sum(ocme_2021_old$EtOH == 1)/nrow(ocme_2021_old), sum(ocme_2022_old$EtOH == 1)/nrow(ocme_2022_old), sum(ocme_2023_old$EtOH == 1)/nrow(ocme_2023_old))

# combine vectors into df
propetoh <- data.frame(year, etohyoung, etohold)

# change the col names to be more informative
names(propetoh) <- c("Year", "Younger", "Older")

# create grouped bar plot, from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/72449952/making-a-grouped-bar-chart-in-r
# getting the labels in the right position from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/37587288/ggplot-label-bars-in-grouped-bar-plot
# info on changing legend title from here https://stackoverflow.com/questions/41649929/how-to-modify-a-legend-title-in-a-barplot-with-ggplot

petoh <- propetoh |>
  # Reshape data to long format
  pivot_longer(Younger:Older) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = Year, y = value, fill = name)) +
  # Implement a grouped bar chart
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = position_dodge(width= 1)) + geom_text(aes(label = round(value, 2)), stat = "identity", vjust = -0.1, colour = "black", size = 9/.pt, position = position_dodge(width= 1)) + theme_light() + ggtitle("Proportion of alcohol-detected deaths by age group in CT, 2018-2023") + ylab("Proportion") + theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)) + scale_fill_discrete(name = "age group") + coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1)) + scale_x_continuous(breaks=propetoh$Year)

petoh

ggsave(plot=petoh, filename = "images/prop_etoh.png", width = 10, height = 8)

```

### Top 5 substance combinations {.tabset}

#### 2018

**Young**

```{r drugsUsedYoung2018, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# got original idea from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/48562288/frequency-of-each-unique-combination-in-data-frame
# the n column wasn't in order, which i fixed with https://dplyr.tidyverse.org/reference/arrange.html
# arrange() provides ascending order so I used desc(n) [instead of just n] to fix that, from https://www.rdocumentation.org/packages/dplyr/versions/0.7.6/topics/desc

mostCommon2018 <- arrange(ocme_2018_young %>% group_by(cocaine, combo..her.pharm.or.fent..OR.pharm.fent, heronly, pharmonly, fentonly, heroin, X6.mam, morphine, hermor_nocod, codeine, cod_w_no_hermor, di.H.codeine, hydromorphone, oxymorphone, hydrocodone, oxycodone, methadone, buprenorphine, fentanyl..4ANPP.too., Frankens, fent.or.frankens, tramadol, opioid.analogs..e.g...U47700., otherop, pharma_w_meth_no_fent.or.op.analogs.or.cod.or..other.op., pharma_nobupnometh, xylazine, gabapentin, benzos, amphetamine, EtOH, weed) %>% tally, desc(n))

# show the top 5 combinations, from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/22471256/overriding-variables-not-shown-in-dplyr-to-display-all-columns-from-df

head(mostCommon2018, 5) %>% glimpse()

```

```{r drugsUsedOld2021, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# show the top 5 combinations
head(mostCommon2021, 5) %>% glimpse()

```

The top 5 substance combinations for older people in 2021 are: 

1) fent only, cocaine
2) fent only, cocaine, alcohol
3) fent only, alcohol

### Injury location {.tabset}


#### 2018

**Young**

```{r injuryYoung2018, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

residence_2018 <- ggplot(data=ocme_2018_young, aes(x=injury_location, ..count..)) + geom_bar(aes(fill = injury_location), position = "dodge") + scale_x_discrete(guide = guide_axis(angle = 45), breaks = ocme_2018_young$injury_location, labels = ocme_2018_young$injury_location) + theme_light() + geom_text(aes(label = ..count..), stat = "count", vjust = 0, colour = "black") + ggtitle("Opioid-detected overdose injury locations for younger people in 2018")+theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5), legend.position="right", axis.text.x = element_text(size = 7))

residence_2018

ggsave(plot=residence_2018, filename = "images/injury_collapsed_young_2018.png", width = 10, height = 8)

residence_2018_prop <- ggplot(data=ocme_2018_young, aes(x=injury_location, ..count..)) + geom_bar(aes(fill = injury_location), position = "dodge") + scale_x_discrete(guide = guide_axis(angle = 45), breaks = ocme_2018_young$injury_location, labels = ocme_2018_young$injury_location) + theme_light() + geom_text(aes(label = round(..count../nrow(ocme_2018_young), 3)), stat = "count", vjust = 0, colour = "black") + ggtitle("Opioid-detected overdose injury locations for younger people in 2018")+theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5), legend.position="none", axis.text.x = element_text(size = 10))

residence_2018_prop

ggsave(plot=residence_2018_prop, filename = "images/injury_collapsed_young_2018_prop.png", width = 10, height = 8)

```

### Town of injury {.tabset}

#### 2018

**Young**


```{r townYoung2018, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
#fixed axis text size in theme() using https://stackoverflow.com/questions/65956833/ggplot2-how-to-dynamically-wrap-resize-rescale-x-axis-labels-so-they-wont-over

town_24h_2018 <- ggplot(data=ocme_2018_young, aes(x=injury_city_revised, ..count..)) + 
      geom_bar(aes(fill = ..count..), position = "dodge") + scale_x_discrete(guide = guide_axis(angle = 45)) + theme_light() + geom_text(aes(label = ..count..), stat = "count", vjust = -0.3, colour = "red", size = 3/.pt) + ggtitle("City/town of OD for 2018 opioid-detected deaths in younger people")+theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5), legend.position="none", axis.text.x = element_text(size = 3))

town_24h_2018

ggsave(plot=town_24h_2018, filename = "images/overdoses_by_town_young_2018.png", width = 10, height = 8)

#find the number of ODs in each town by aggregating the indicator var for each town, from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/60961960/how-do-i-sum-a-column-with-categorical-vairables-in-r

# create a new dataframe that we can manipulate without messing up within24h2018

young2018prop <- ocme_2018_young %>% group_by(injury_city_revised) %>% summarise_at(vars(fatal), sum)

# find towns that don't have anyone discovered within 24h and add them into the df
# i have to use unique() so I don't get repeats

missingtowns2018 <- setdiff(unique(ocme_2018$injury_city_revised), young2018prop$injury_city_revised)

for (i in missingtowns2018) {
  
  # create row for that town and a 0 next to number of fatalities discovered in 24h
  newtown <- c(i, 0)
  
  # add to within24h2018prop
  young2018prop = rbind(young2018prop, newtown)
  
}

# convert the within24h2018prop fatals into numerics because for some reason they're strings
young2018prop$fatal <- as.numeric(young2018prop$fatal)

# aggregate fatalities for overall deaths [not just discovered in 24h]
ocme_2018_agg <- ocme_2018 %>% group_by(injury_city_revised) %>% summarise_at(vars(fatal), sum)

# rename the danbury_2018_agg24h "fatal" column because it'll get confusing otherwise when merged
names(ocme_2018_agg)[names(ocme_2018_agg) == 'fatal'] <- 'total'

# merge with within24h2018prop to have a column with the actual number of deaths
ocme_2018_young_merged <- merge(young2018prop, ocme_2018_agg, by="injury_city_revised")

# get the proportion of fatalities discovered in 24h, multiply by 100 so we have a percentage
ocme_2018_young_merged$Prop <- round((ocme_2018_young_merged$fatal/ocme_2018_young_merged$total)*100, digits=2)

# convert any NaN to 0 -- from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/18142117/how-to-replace-nan-value-with-zero-in-a-huge-data-frame

ocme_2018_young_merged$Prop[is.nan(ocme_2018_young_merged$Prop)] <- 0

# Plot the proportion of people discovered within 24h
# had an issue with the fill, edited with http://www.sthda.com/english/wiki/ggplot2-barplots-quick-start-guide-r-software-and-data-visualization
# needed to change the font size for the text overlay, used https://stackoverflow.com/questions/25061822/ggplot-geom-text-font-size-control

town_2018_young_capita <- ggplot(data=ocme_2018_young_merged, aes(x=injury_city_revised, y=Prop, fill=Prop, position = "dodge")) + 
      geom_bar(stat="Identity") + scale_x_discrete(guide = guide_axis(angle = 45)) + theme_light() + geom_text(aes(label = Prop), vjust = -0.3, colour = "red", size = 3/.pt) + ggtitle("Percent of fatalities in younger people by town in 2018")+theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5), legend.position="none", axis.text.x = element_text(size = 3))

town_2018_young_capita

ggsave(plot=town_2018_young_capita, filename = "images/overdoses_by_town_prop_young_2018.png", width = 10, height = 8)

```

```{r townYoungSWORD2020, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
#fixed axis text size in theme() using https://stackoverflow.com/questions/65956833/ggplot2-how-to-dynamically-wrap-resize-rescale-x-axis-labels-so-they-wont-over

town_24h_2020 <- ggplot(data=sword_2020_young, aes(x=City, ..count..)) + 
      geom_bar(aes(fill = ..count..), position = "dodge") + scale_x_discrete(guide = guide_axis(angle = 45)) + theme_light() + geom_text(aes(label = ..count..), stat = "count", vjust = -0.3, colour = "red", size = 3/.pt) + ggtitle("City/town of OD for 2020 suspected nonfatal opioid-involved overdoses \n in younger people")+theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5), legend.position="none", axis.text.x = element_text(size = 3))

town_24h_2020

ggsave(plot=town_24h_2020, filename = "images/overdoses_by_town_young_sword_2020.png", width = 10, height = 8)

#find the number of ODs in each town by aggregating the indicator var for each town, from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/60961960/how-do-i-sum-a-column-with-categorical-vairables-in-r

# create a new dataframe that we can manipulate without messing up within24h2018

young2020prop <- sword_2020_young %>% group_by(City) %>% summarise_at(vars(Nonfatal), sum)

# find towns that don't have anyone discovered within 24h and add them into the df
# i have to use unique() so I don't get repeats

missingtowns2020 <- setdiff(unique(sword_2020$City), young2020prop$City)

for (i in missingtowns2020) {
  
  # create row for that town and a 0 next to number of fatalities discovered in 24h
  newtown <- c(i, 0)
  
  # add to within24h2018prop
  young2020prop = rbind(young2020prop, newtown)
  
}

# convert the within24h2018prop fatals into numerics because for some reason they're strings
young2020prop$Nonfatal <- as.numeric(young2020prop$Nonfatal)

# aggregate fatalities for overall deaths [not just discovered in 24h]
sword_2020_agg <- sword_2020 %>% group_by(City) %>% summarise_at(vars(Nonfatal), sum)

# rename the danbury_2018_agg24h "fatal" column because it'll get confusing otherwise when merged
names(sword_2020_agg)[names(sword_2020_agg) == 'Nonfatal'] <- 'total'

# merge with within24h2018prop to have a column with the actual number of deaths
sword_2020_young_merged <- merge(young2020prop, sword_2020_agg, by="City")

# get the proportion of fatalities discovered in 24h, multiply by 100 so we have a percentage
sword_2020_young_merged$Prop <- round((sword_2020_young_merged$Nonfatal/sword_2020_young_merged$total)*100, digits=2)

# convert any NaN to 0 -- from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/18142117/how-to-replace-nan-value-with-zero-in-a-huge-data-frame

sword_2020_young_merged$Prop[is.nan(sword_2020_young_merged$Prop)] <- 0

# Plot the proportion of people discovered within 24h
# had an issue with the fill, edited with http://www.sthda.com/english/wiki/ggplot2-barplots-quick-start-guide-r-software-and-data-visualization
# needed to change the font size for the text overlay, used https://stackoverflow.com/questions/25061822/ggplot-geom-text-font-size-control

town_2020_young_capita <- ggplot(data=sword_2020_young_merged, aes(x=City, y=Prop, fill=Prop, position = "dodge")) + 
      geom_bar(stat="Identity") + scale_x_discrete(guide = guide_axis(angle = 45)) + theme_light() + geom_text(aes(label = Prop), vjust = -0.3, colour = "red", size = 3/.pt) + ggtitle("Percent of suspected nonfatal overdoses in younger people by town in 2020")+theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5), legend.position="none", axis.text.x = element_text(size = 3))

town_2020_young_capita

ggsave(plot=town_2020_young_capita, filename = "images/overdoses_by_town_prop_young_sword_2020.png", width = 10, height = 8)
```

```{r townOldSWORD2021, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
town_24h_2021

ggsave(plot=town_24h_2021, filename = "images/overdoses_by_town_old_sword_2021.png", width = 10, height = 8)

#find the number of ODs in each town by aggregating the indicator var for each town, from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/60961960/how-do-i-sum-a-column-with-categorical-vairables-in-r

# create a new dataframe that we can manipulate without messing up within24h2018

old2021prop <- sword_2021_old %>% group_by(City) %>% summarise_at(vars(Nonfatal), sum)

# find towns that don't have anyone discovered within 24h and add them into the df
# i have to use unique() so I don't get repeats

missingtowns2021 <- setdiff(unique(sword_2021$City), old2021prop$City)

for (i in missingtowns2021) {
  
  # create row for that town and a 0 next to number of fatalities discovered in 24h
  newtown <- c(i, 0)
  
  # add to within24h2018prop
  old2021prop = rbind(old2021prop, newtown)
  
}

# convert the within24h2018prop fatals into numerics because for some reason they're strings
old2021prop$Nonfatal <- as.numeric(old2021prop$Nonfatal)

# aggregate fatalities for overall deaths [not just discovered in 24h]
sword_2021_agg <- sword_2021 %>% group_by(City) %>% summarise_at(vars(Nonfatal), sum)

# rename the danbury_2018_agg24h "Nonfatal" column because it'll get confusing otherwise when merged
names(sword_2021_agg)[names(sword_2021_agg) == 'Nonfatal'] <- 'total'

# merge with within24h2018prop to have a column with the actual number of deaths
sword_2021_old_merged <- merge(old2021prop, sword_2021_agg, by="City")

# get the proportion of fatalities discovered in 24h, multiply by 100 so we have a percentage
sword_2021_old_merged$Prop <- round((sword_2021_old_merged$Nonfatal/sword_2021_old_merged$total)*100, digits=2)

# convert any NaN to 0 -- from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/18142117/how-to-replace-nan-value-with-zero-in-a-huge-data-frame

sword_2021_old_merged$Prop[is.nan(sword_2021_old_merged$Prop)] <- 0

# Plot the proportion of people discovered within 24h
# had an issue with the fill, edited with http://www.sthda.com/english/wiki/ggplot2-barplots-quick-start-guide-r-software-and-data-visualization
# needed to change the font size for the text overlay, used https://stackoverflow.com/questions/25061822/ggplot-geom-text-font-size-control

town_2021_old_capita <- ggplot(data=sword_2021_old_merged, aes(x=City, y=Prop, fill=Prop, position = "dodge")) + 
      geom_bar(stat="Identity") + scale_x_discrete(guide = guide_axis(angle = 45)) + theme_light() + geom_text(aes(label = Prop), vjust = -0.3, colour = "red", size = 3/.pt) + ggtitle("Percent of suspected nonfatal overdoses in older people by town in 2021")+theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5), legend.position="none", axis.text.x = element_text(size = 3))

town_2021_old_capita

ggsave(plot=town_2021_old_capita, filename = "images/overdoses_by_town_prop_old_sword_2021.png", width = 10, height = 8)
```

```{r townYoungSWORD2023, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
  # create row for that town and a 0 next to number of fatalities discovered in 24h
  newtown <- c(i, 0)
  
  # add to within24h2018prop
  young2023prop = rbind(young2023prop, newtown)
  
}

# convert the within24h2018prop fatals into numerics because for some reason they're strings
young2023prop$Nonfatal <- as.numeric(young2023prop$Nonfatal)

# aggregate fatalities for overall deaths [not just discovered in 24h]
sword_2023_agg <- sword_2023 %>% group_by(City) %>% summarise_at(vars(Nonfatal), sum)

# rename the danbury_2018_agg24h "fatal" column because it'll get confusing otherwise when merged
names(sword_2023_agg)[names(sword_2023_agg) == 'Nonfatal'] <- 'total'

# merge with within24h2018prop to have a column with the actual number of deaths
sword_2023_young_merged <- merge(young2023prop, sword_2023_agg, by="City")

# get the proportion of fatalities discovered in 24h, multiply by 100 so we have a percentage
sword_2023_young_merged$Prop <- round((sword_2023_young_merged$Nonfatal/sword_2023_young_merged$total)*100, digits=2)

# convert any NaN to 0 -- from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/18142117/how-to-replace-nan-value-with-zero-in-a-huge-data-frame

sword_2023_young_merged$Prop[is.nan(sword_2023_young_merged$Prop)] <- 0

# Plot the proportion of people discovered within 24h
# had an issue with the fill, edited with http://www.sthda.com/english/wiki/ggplot2-barplots-quick-start-guide-r-software-and-data-visualization
# needed to change the font size for the text overlay, used https://stackoverflow.com/questions/25061822/ggplot-geom-text-font-size-control

town_2023_young_capita <- ggplot(data=sword_2023_young_merged, aes(x=City, y=Prop, fill=Prop, position = "dodge")) + 
      geom_bar(stat="Identity") + scale_x_discrete(guide = guide_axis(angle = 45)) + theme_light() + geom_text(aes(label = Prop), vjust = -0.3, colour = "red", size = 3/.pt) + ggtitle("Percent of suspected nonfatal overdoses in younger people by town in 2023")+theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5), legend.position="none", axis.text.x = element_text(size = 3))

town_2023_young_capita

ggsave(plot=town_2023_young_capita, filename = "images/overdoses_by_town_prop_young_sword_2023.png", width = 10, height = 8)

```

### Maps of OD towns {.tabset} 

#### 2018

**Young**

```{r town2018MapYoung, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
#find the number of ODs in each town by aggregating the indicator var for each town, from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/60961960/how-do-i-sum-a-column-with-categorical-vairables-in-r

ocme_2018_counts<- ocme_2018_young %>% group_by(injury_city_revised) %>% summarise_at(vars(fatal), sum)

#rename the injury city variable so we can merge it with the ct_towns df

colnames(ocme_2018_counts) <- c('NAME', 'Fatal')

# not all towns experienced an OD in 2020. Check which: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/72274729/find-elements-in-a-column-that-is-not-in-another-column-of-another-dataframe-in

ocme_2018_odcounts <- data.frame(setdiff(ct_towns$NAME, ocme_2018_counts$NAME), 0)

# give this the same column names as ocme_2020_counts

colnames(ocme_2018_odcounts) <- c('NAME', 'Fatal')

# merge the two datasets

ocme_2018_counts <- rbind(ocme_2018_counts, ocme_2018_odcounts)

#merge with ct_towns so that way we can use the fatal OD counts for the fill

ct_town_odcounts_2018 <- merge(ct_towns, ocme_2018_counts,by="NAME")

# Plot! And use the fatal data to color the plot in. Info from https://geanders.github.io/navy_public_health/3-2-basic-mapping.html

map_2018 <- ggplot(ocme_2018_young) + theme_void() + geom_sf(data=ct_town_odcounts_2018, size=0.1, aes(fill=Fatal))+ ggtitle("Fatal opioid-detected overdoses in younger people by town in 2018")+scale_fill_viridis_c(option="plasma")+theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5), legend.position="right")

map_2018

#save this one for the presentation
ggsave(plot=map_2018, filename = "images/map_2018_young.png", width = 10, height = 8)


```

### Injury town v. residence town {.tabset}

I chose towns based on either what regional harm reduction workers wanted, based on towns with overdose prevention infrastructure or based on towns with the most ODs in the past few years. I can change this easily to show all towns. I'm looking at instances where people who OD'd in a town didn't live there -- I am referring to this as "out-of-town ODs."

#### 2018

**Young**

```{r injuryResidence2018Young, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# get rid of blank/unknown injury and residence locations, from https://www.r-bloggers.com/2022/05/subsetting-with-multiple-conditions-in-r/

ocme_2018_noblank <- ocme_2018_young %>% filter(residence_city_updated != "" & injury_city_revised!="Unknown")

# convert all Willimantic residences to Windham, because otherwise the out of town calculations get messed up
ocme_2018_noblank$residence_city_updated <- ifelse(ocme_2018_noblank$residence_city_updated == "Willimantic", "Windham", ocme_2018_noblank$residence_city_updated)

# print a statement with some function output -- from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/13036649/how-do-i-concatenate-string-and-an-output-evaluated-from-a-function-in-r [the %d stands for an integer]

sprintf("There were %d instances where a person's residence town didn't match up with their injury town, out of %d ODs in younger people in 2018 where the injury and residence town were both known. This is %f of all such ODs in this year.", nrow(subset(ocme_2022_noblank, Res.City != injury_city_revised)), nrow(ocme_2022_noblank), nrow(subset(ocme_2022_noblank, Res.City != injury_city_revised))/nrow(ocme_2022_noblank))
```

```{r injuryResidence2022Young, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# for some reason for this you need double backslashes instead of single
#write.csv(big4_2022,"C:\\Users\\ar2529\\Desktop\\opioid_causal_effect\\2022_out_of_town.csv", row.names = FALSE) 

print("Here's a more in-depth look at out-of-town ODs for younger people in specific towns:")

# initialize empty matrix, from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/32712301/create-empty-data-frame-with-column-names-by-assigning-a-string-vector

out_of_town_2022 <- data.frame(matrix(ncol = 4, nrow = 0))
cols <- c("Town name","Out-of-town ODs","Total ODs","Percent of out-of-town ODs")

# iteratively add info from these towns to the df, from https://www.projectpro.io/recipes/append-output-from-for-loop-dataframe-r

# change to unique(ocme_2022$injury_city_revised) to get all towns -- from https://stackoverflow.com/questions/45235422/does-r-have-a-set-data-structure

for (i in c("Danbury", "Waterbury", "Torrington", "New Haven", "West Haven", "Hartford", "Norwich", "New London", "Bridgeport", "New Britain", "Litchfield", "Meriden", "Norwalk", "Stamford", "Windham")) {
  
  # subset for the number of ODs in that town 
  
  ocme_injury_2022 <- subset(ocme_2022_noblank, injury_city_revised == i)
  
  # create a results vector to append to out_of_town 2020 df
  # contains town name, number of ODs from out of town residents, total ODs and fraction of out of town ODs in that   order
  
  results <- c(i, nrow(subset(ocme_injury_2022, Res.City != injury_city_revised)), nrow(ocme_injury_2022), round(nrow(subset(ocme_injury_2022, Res.City != injury_city_revised))/nrow(ocme_injury_2022), 3)*100)
  
  # convert NaN to 0
  results[is.nan(results)] <- 0

  # add this to the out of town df 
  out_of_town_2022 = rbind(out_of_town_2022, results)
}

# for some reason it doesn't work if I do this before adding rows?
colnames(out_of_town_2022) <- cols

out_of_town_2022
```

```{r ownHome2018, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
sprintf("The proportion of younger decedents ODing in their own residence was %f and the proportion of older decedents ODing in their own residence was %f.", sum(ocme_2018_young$injury_address_updated == ocme_2018_young$residence_address_updated)/nrow(ocme_2018_young), sum(ocme_2018_old$injury_address_updated == ocme_2018_old$residence_address_updated)/nrow(ocme_2018_old))
```
